name: FAIRsharing registry search/API
tool_type: database, standard and policy registry query API
input_ids: database or standard name|research domain|FAIRsharing record ID
input_formats: web query|REST/JSON or GraphQL request as permitted
outputs: registry records|resource relationships|standard and policy descriptions
main_use: Discover and compare microbiome databases, research data repositories, standards and policies; follow record links to the resource owner.
limitations: This is a metadata registry, not a dataset API. API_doc rendered only a JavaScript shell in this review; authentication, query behavior and full pagination were not tested. Follow current FAIRsharing API terms before programmatic or bulk use.
license: CC BY-SA 4.0 for FAIRsharing content; API-specific terms apply

name: re3data REST API v4 and repository XML export
tool_type: research repository registry search API
outputs: repository metadata|access modes|content types|standards|certifications|persistent identifier details
main_use: Search repository-level records and inspect a repository's data access, content and metadata-standard information; supports repository landscape discovery.
limitations: Returns repository descriptions, not microbiome datasets or sample records. Follow each repository link and check its own policies and data catalog.
license: CC0 for re3data metadata; repository data terms are independent

name: bio.tools REST API
tool_type: life-science software and service registry search API
input_ids: tool name|function|domain|EDAM topic or operation|bio.tools ID
outputs: tool descriptions|inputs|outputs|versions|licenses|documentation links
main_use: Discover software, services and database tools; filter by functions and supported data types, then follow official documentation/source links.
limitations: Registry metadata only; it does not install or run tools and does not return underlying sample data. Search is fuzzy unless exact-match parameters are quoted; read endpoints are public, write endpoints require authentication.
license: bio.tools registry terms; each listed tool has its own license

name: MGnify REST API v2
tool_type: microbiome sample, study and analysis query API
outputs: study|sample|run|biome|analysis records and relationships
main_use: Query MGnify's ENA-linked microbiome studies, samples, runs and analysis results programmatically using the current v2 API.
limitations: API v1 was deprecated in 2026-06 and is frozen; documentation says it will be switched off no earlier than 2026-09-01. Check current v2 docs and preserve the upstream source for each metadata field. Publication-level annotations are not automatically sample-level facts.
license: EBI/ENA data and API terms apply

name: Microbiome Repo static metadata API and releases
tool_type: evidence-linked human microbiome study/sample metadata discovery
input_ids: BioProject accession|condition code|intervention code|age category|search term
outputs: project/sample/run metadata|evidence routes|confidence|field coverage
main_use: Find and retrieve evidence-linked metadata for curated human shotgun DNA/RNA studies; prefer project-scoped JSON/CSV endpoints when one study is the target.
limitations: Coverage is release-bounded and currently focuses on human-associated shotgun DNA/RNA. Check release and terms; sample rows are not participants, and each source claim must retain its evidence route/confidence. Does not replace archive or paper verification.

name: Entrez Direct (EDirect)
tool_type: NCBI metadata/query CLI
outputs: XML/JSON/TSV metadata and linked IDs
main_use: Command-line access to NCBI Entrez search, fetch, summary and link functions; useful for batch metadata and literature/accession cross-references
limitations: Entrez fields are only as complete as the submitting record; EDirect is not a supplementary-file or clinical metadata recovery tool. Follow NCBI usage and rate limits; it does not download FASTQ reads.

name: NCBI SRA Toolkit
tool_type: sequence download and conversion CLI
outputs: SRA files|FASTQ|SAM
main_use: Use prefetch to retrieve SRA Run data and fasterq-dump/sam-dump to convert it to common sequence formats
limitations: Primarily sequence-data download/conversion, not a metadata enrichment tool. Run files do not contain linked sample metadata; plan temporary disk space and follow public/controlled access policy.
license: US Government Work/public use; see repository notice

name: PySRAdb
tool_type: metadata CLI and Python API
input_ids: SRA study|experiment|sample|run accession; optional GEO accession
outputs: tabular metadata, linked accessions, download command previews
main_use: Query SRA/EBI metadata and expose study/experiment/sample/run fields in CLI or Python; useful for batch inspection and accession crosswalks
limitations: Output depends on upstream SRA/EBI fields and API behavior; does not guarantee recovery of details only reported in papers or supplements. Validate sample-to-subject mappings independently.

name: NMDC Runtime API
tool_type: REST API
input_ids: NMDC study ID|NMDC biosample ID|data object ID
outputs: JSON study, biosample, data-object and workflow metadata
main_use: Programmatically search and retrieve standardized environmental microbiome metadata and links to NMDC data objects; the API documents GET endpoints for studies, biosamples, and data objects.
limitations: NMDC does not support human microbiome data. Some downloads or endpoints require ORCID authentication; dataset availability is limited to NMDC-contributed records and is not a universal archive resolver.
license: NMDC data use policy: CC BY 4.0

name: JGI Data Portal API
tool_type: REST API
outputs: file metadata|downloadable public data|archive retrieval requests
main_use: Search JGI public genome/metagenome file metadata and automate file retrieval through the JGI API.
limitations: The API docs require a signed-in Data Portal session; the API is a work in progress. Some files are in long-term tape archive and must be queued. It covers JGI data, not arbitrary public microbiome accessions.
license: See JGI portal and dataset-specific terms

name: PanGBank REST API
tool_type: REST API
outputs: pangenome graph and associated genome/gene metadata
main_use: Programmatic access to PanGBank precomputed prokaryotic pangenomes and associated resources.
limitations: Comparative genomics resource, not a sample metadata resolver; API behavior, rate limits, and response schema should be confirmed against current documentation.
license: API/software CeCILL v2.1; datasets CC BY-SA 4.0

name: BacDive REST API v2
tool_type: REST API
outputs: JSON strain record with taxonomy, phenotype, origin, culture and sequence metadata
main_use: Retrieve structured strain-level records from BacDive for microbial isolate identification and reference context.
limitations: API v2 fields and access policy should be checked against current docs; strain-level records do not resolve host-cohort sample IDs or participant phenotypes.

name: MetaHQ CLI
tool_type: metadata annotation and retrieval CLI
outputs: CSV/TSV/Parquet/JSON sample- or series-level annotations with source citations
main_use: Retrieve evidence-linked tissue, disease, sex and age annotations from the MetaHQ curation database; filter annotation sources by evidence level and license, and export source/citation metadata.
limitations: General omics tool whose documented examples focus on human/mouse RNA-seq and microarray, not microbiome amplicon/shotgun. It queries MetaHQ's curated corpus rather than arbitrary accession strings; annotation database is CC BY-NC 4.0 while CLI software is BSD-3-Clause. 2026 preprint is not peer-reviewed.
license: Database CC BY-NC 4.0; CLI BSD-3-Clause; source-specific terms apply

name: ffq
tool_type: multi-archive accession metadata retrieval CLI
outputs: JSON metadata for input and linked downstream accessions; raw-data download links
main_use: Resolve a public sequencing accession across GEO, SRA, ENA, DDBJ, and BioSample, returning linked records down to run level; can also accept a paper DOI and emit raw data URLs.
limitations: Only retrieves fields exposed by upstream archives and does not recover article/supplement-only host variables; the current repository warns that NCBI .SRA links may be deprecated and can yield empty output for the --ncbi option. Test the selected provider and output level for the project.

name: SRA Explorer
tool_type: web dataset search and download helper
outputs: full metadata table; ENA FastQ URLs; SRA download links; bash download script; optional Seqera dataset
main_use: Search SRA datasets, review full metadata, select runs and generate download links or a sample dataset for Seqera Platform.
limitations: The project author describes it as a small exploratory web app and recommends more scalable/stable CLI alternatives; ENA may repeat one SRA run for multiple FASTQ entries. Current query results were not end-to-end tested.

name: fastq-dl
tool_type: accession metadata and FASTQ retrieval CLI
outputs: ENA-derived metadata; FASTQ files; logs and checksum validation
main_use: Resolve an ENA/SRA accession through ENA Data Warehouse metadata and download FASTQ for associated Runs; supports metadata-only mode and grouping by Sample or Experiment.
limitations: Optimized for read retrieval, not publication or supplement mining; ENA-derived metadata may lack host lifestyle/clinical fields and group-by-sample can merge many biologically distinct Runs if the archive links them to one Sample.

name: ENA Browser Tools
tool_type: ENA metadata and data download CLI
outputs: ENA XML metadata; FASTQ/SRA/submitted files; grouped Study/Sample downloads
main_use: Use enaDataGet/enaGroupGet to retrieve accession files and optionally download Run/Analysis XML metadata; supports sample/study-level grouped download.
limitations: ENA-centered and designed for data/file retrieval; XML represents archive records and does not add host traits absent from ENA. Check release compatibility, file size, and output path before bulk downloads.

name: nf-core/fetchngs
tool_type: Nextflow metadata and read retrieval pipeline
input_formats: one accession per line in CSV/text
outputs: curated ENA metadata samplesheet; FASTQ files; run accessions and download checksums
main_use: Batch-resolve supported public repository identifiers to experiment/run records, fetch ENA metadata, produce a samplesheet and download raw FastQ for downstream pipelines.
limitations: Designed to prepare raw reads for analysis and requires Nextflow plus a container/profile setup; archive-derived samplesheet fields need manual review and do not recover publication/supplement-only host variables.

name: Kingfisher
tool_type: public sequencing metadata and read retrieval CLI
outputs: Run metadata table (human-readable|CSV|TSV|JSON|Feather|Parquet)|FASTQ|SRA|FASTA files
main_use: Use annotate to retrieve run metadata from NCBI, including optional extended columns; use get to obtain public reads from ENA, NCBI, AWS or GCP with fallback providers.
limitations: Metadata remains limited to upstream archive fields; default annotation output is brief unless --all-columns is used. NCBI API rate limits apply to repeated/parallel calls. Does not retrieve paper supplements or infer host/sample crosswalks.

name: iSeq
tool_type: multi-archive accession metadata and sequencing-data CLI
outputs: archive metadata|FASTQ|FASTQ.GZ|SRA|BAM|download and MD5 logs
main_use: Resolve supported accession formats across GSA, SRA, ENA and DDBJ, retrieve metadata, choose a download source and verify file checksums.
limitations: Metadata and ID links depend on source archive contents and current endpoint behavior. Read retrieval may require substantial storage/bandwidth; it does not recover paper-only host variables or participant crosswalks.

name: metatools_ncbi
tool_type: NCBI BioSample and SRA RunInfo metadata CLI
outputs: BioSample JSON metadata|SRA RunInfo metadata|best-effort accession-to-BioSample mapping
main_use: Download BioSample metadata and RunInfo metadata for supplied sample lists or taxa; attempt to resolve supported NCBI identifiers to BioSample.
limitations: Repository changelog is old and explicitly notes slow conversion; a BioProject linked to many BioSamples cannot be mapped to one unique sample. Current API compatibility and installation should be confirmed before batch use; no paper/supplement mining.

name: grabseqs
tool_type: microbiome-focused public read and metadata CLI
input_formats: one or more IDs|bulk project IDs
outputs: metadata CSV|sample/run list|FASTQ.GZ reads
main_use: Bulk-download reads and corresponding repository metadata from NCBI SRA or MG-RAST; supports listing samples before download and retries.
limitations: Current v1.0 removed iMicrobe support. A reported SRA metadata issue can omit some BioSample attributes; verify export fields. Requires download dependencies and does not mine papers or supplements.

name: GEOfastq
tool_type: GEO-to-ENA FASTQ retrieval R package
outputs: retrieved GEO/SRA sample metadata for resolution|SRA Run IDs|ENA FASTQ links/files
main_use: Use a GEO accession to retrieve related GEO/SRA sample metadata, identify Run accessions and obtain ENA FASTQ files.
limitations: Specialized GEO-to-ENA workflow; it does not produce a comprehensive host phenotype table and may not work when ENA FASTQs or archive links are absent. Does not inspect article supplements.

name: NCBI SRA Run Selector
tool_type: official NCBI archive search and metadata-export web tool
outputs: filtered Run table|RunInfo table (TSV)|Run accession list
main_use: Search and filter Runs linked to studies, samples or experiments; export selected RunInfo metadata or accession lists through the official NCBI web interface.
limitations: Exports available archive metadata at Run scope; Run rows are not participants/biological samples and fields do not include paper-only phenotype data. Controlled dbGaP data remain subject to approval.

name: Redbiom
tool_type: microbiome sample and feature search CLI
input_ids: Qiita study/sample metadata|taxon or feature|metadata predicates
outputs: matching sample IDs|sample metadata|BIOM feature tables
main_use: Search Qiita (including EMP) samples by sample metadata or biological features, retrieve matched metadata and observation data, and support discovery by habitat or assay context.
limitations: Coverage is limited to data indexed in Qiita and available contexts; metadata labels and query terms require inspection; sample information, preparation and processed-feature contexts are distinct; not a general arbitrary BioSample resolver.

name: MetaSUB map_collate
tool_type: project-specific sample ID mapping and metadata collation package
input_ids: MetaSUB sample name|H.A. identifier|barcode|plate position|FASTQ filename
outputs: collated sample metadata table|resolved identifier relationships
main_use: Collate MetaSUB metadata from documentary source files and follow multiple layers of sample-name indirection to connect metadata with sequencing filenames.
limitations: Project-specific best-effort matching, dependent on heterogeneous source tables and prior cleaning; source README documents incomplete fields and ID/data-quality problems, including barcodes with lost leading zeros. Not a general accession resolver and matches require audit.

name: HuMMANet R/Bioconductor package
tool_type: study-level paired microbiome-metabolome data access package
outputs: MultiAssayExperiment study bundle|sample metadata|taxa abundance|original/harmonized metabolite matrices|annotation tables
main_use: Discover studies and retrieve linked metadata, microbiome and metabolomics profiles, and metabolite annotations through a consistent Bioconductor interface.
limitations: Limited to the studies and modalities bundled by HuMMANet; not an arbitrary accession-to-sample resolver. Source studies may have different access terms and not all raw source data are redistributed.
license: See package and source repository license

name: IGS Portal Client
tool_type: manifest-based data download CLI for GDC-based portals
outputs: selected data files with checksum validation
main_use: Download selected HMBR files using a cart-generated manifest; the manifest can include file IDs, checksums, sizes, URLs and associated HMBR sample IDs.
limitations: Downloads files described by the manifest; it does not search or interpret metadata. Check file-level access type and source terms; credentials or cloud configuration may be needed for some endpoint types.

name: NIAID Data Ecosystem Discovery API
tool_type: cross-repository resource and dataset metadata search API
input_formats: REST API query|CSV or JSON metadata download
outputs: filtered resource/dataset/tool metadata records
main_use: Search the NIAID Data Ecosystem index programmatically and retrieve metadata for datasets, resource catalogs and computational tools; supports follow-through to source repositories.
limitations: The API searches the portal's indexed sources, not all public data repositories; it does not host source data or bypass registration/controlled-access requirements. Returned metadata can be incomplete or unrelated to microbiome studies; validate each source record.

name: metaTraits JSON API
tool_type: REST API
input_ids: NCBI taxonomy ID|list of taxonomy IDs
outputs: Taxonomy-level microbial trait observations and summaries in JSON
main_use: Retrieve one or multiple taxonomy-linked trait records and cite source provenance; optional database filters separate source sets.
limitations: API schema and limits are documented, but services were under scheduled maintenance at the time of checking. Traits are microbial taxa/genome traits and do not provide host participant metadata.
license: Source database and prediction-model terms apply

name: MetaVR API
tool_type: REST API
outputs: Filtered viral genome, metagenome, protein-cluster and metadata records
main_use: Programmatically search and retrieve MetaVR viral sequence catalog records and associated contextual fields.
limitations: Official paper documents the API, but the portal/API endpoint returned access errors in this check; endpoint behavior and limits need revalidation. Not a host cohort metadata resolver.

name: VirJenDB REST API
tool_type: REST API
outputs: Filtered viral sequence records, downloadable metadata, sequences, and metadata schema
main_use: Search, filter, and download harmonized viral sequence metadata with links back to NCBI, BV-BRC, ICTV, and related sources.
limitations: Official docs describe Search, Download, and Metadata endpoint groups; this round confirmed the indexed portal release and metadata schema but could not parse or call Swagger. Individual host fields can be absent or unstandardized and should be provenance-checked.

name: AMRnet API and snapshots
tool_type: REST API|tabular snapshots
outputs: Per-organism TSV downloads, weekly public CSV snapshots, and REST API records
main_use: Retrieve public genome-level metadata and AMR surveillance summaries for supported pathogens.
limitations: Limited to supported organisms and fields required for AMR surveillance; does not represent general microbiome or clinical phenotypes. Dashboard/S3 download is public without registration; REST API requires a free API key. No file or API request was made in this round.
license: See AMRnet/source-data terms; API requires free key, TSV/S3 snapshots are public

name: mOTUs profiler and database download CLI
tool_type: microbial taxonomic profiling and genome download CLI
outputs: taxonomic profile|genome sequences|annotations
main_use: Profile short-read metagenomes and query/download genomes or annotations associated with mOTUs-db records
limitations: Requires local reads for profiling; taxonomy/genome context does not restore participant metadata. Check database/tool version and download scope.

name: OmicsMLRepoR
tool_type: R package for harmonized metadata download and ontology-based search
outputs: harmonized sample metadata table|ontology-filtered records
main_use: Download and browse harmonized cMD metadata using normalized fields and ontology-aware search, including synonyms and descendants
limitations: Current supported metadata sources are curatedMetagenomicData and cBioPortalData; not a generic accession resolver and does not search arbitrary papers or supplements.

name: PRIME REST API v1 and primeDB R client
tool_type: microbiome metadata and abundance API/R client
input_ids: Project accession|Run ID|sample ID|phenotype or taxonomy query
input_formats: REST JSON|R function arguments|CSV/TSV accession list
outputs: project/sample metadata|taxonomy tables|observed and relative abundance|custom abundance tables
main_use: Search, retrieve, filter and download PRIME human 16S metadata and abundance profiles programmatically using a versioned REST API or the primeDB R package
limitations: Limited to PRIME included human-associated 16S studies. Sample records are not participant counts; API availability/rate policies and dataset license must be checked at use time. Does not recover unsubmitted paper supplements.
license: MIT per PRIME paper; academic-use dataset terms should be checked separately

name: NFDI4Health Health Study Hub REST API
tool_type: health study metadata discovery API
outputs: published health-study resource metadata|related variables/documents/access information
main_use: Search the Health Study Hub published resource catalog programmatically through its documented REST API
limitations: General clinical/public-health/epidemiology scope, not microbiome-specific. Search results point to source research; they do not guarantee microbiome assay, BioSample/Run mapping, or access to individual-level data. API request was not executed in this review.
license: API/data use according to Health Study Hub and each source-record terms
